Build an agrinutri soil input stack from SoilGrids (open global default)

Source: R/soilgrids_input.R
soilgrids_input.Rd

Downloads the soil properties that the agrinutri nitrogen balance consumes from the ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0 service and returns them as a terra::SpatRaster with the layer names, units and shape that spatial_N_balance() and farm_balance() expect. It is the open, global fallback soil layer: with it the whole agrinutri pipeline (balance, prescription mean and uncertainty) runs end to end on freely licensed data (CC-BY 4.0) anywhere on Earth, without a proprietary local soil map.

Usage

soilgrids_input(
  aoi,
  depths = c("0-5", "5-15", "15-30"),
  crs_out = NULL,
  template = NULL,
  uncertainty = FALSE,
  buffer = 500
)

Arguments

aoi

Area of interest: an sf/sfc object, a terra::SpatVector, or a path to a vector file readable by terra::vect. Its extent (buffered) is downloaded.

depths

Character vector of SoilGrids depth intervals to combine into a thickness-weighted topsoil value. Defaults to the 0 to 30 cm topsoil (c("0-5", "5-15", "15-30")). Accepted: "0-5", "5-15", "15-30", "30-60", "60-100", "100-200".

crs_out

Target coordinate reference system for the returned stack (anything terra::crs accepts). Defaults to the CRS of aoi (or of template when supplied).

template

Optional terra::SpatRaster whose grid the output is resampled to (for alignment with a field raster). Note that resampling a 250 m product to a finer grid does not add spatial detail.

uncertainty

Logical; if TRUE, also download the Q0.05 and Q0.95 quantiles and append per-property standard-deviation layers (Clay_sd, Sand_sd, TN_sd, SOM_sd, approximated as (Q0.95 - Q0.05) / 3.29 in converted units) for use as the input error of a Monte-Carlo propagation.

buffer

Numeric buffer (in metres) added around the AOI extent before cropping, so edge pixels are not lost. Default 500.

Value

A terra::SpatRaster with layers TN (g/kg), SOM (percent), Clay (percent), Sand (percent) and CNratio (dimensionless), masked to aoi and in crs_out; plus the four *_sd layers when uncertainty = TRUE. The result is ready to pass as the soil_stack argument of spatial_N_balance().

Details

SoilGrids is a 250 m global product with modest local accuracy (global cross-validation model efficiency about 0.5 for total nitrogen and 0.65 for organic carbon), so it drives the field-mean regulatory dose and the farm total, not the within-field 10 m pattern. Treat it as an open default and a benchmark for the value of local sampling, not as a validated field input.

Unit conversions applied to the raw SoilGrids values (as returned by geodata): clay and sand from g/kg to percent (divide by 10); total nitrogen from cg/kg to g/kg (divide by 100); organic carbon from dg/kg to g/kg (divide by 10); soil organic matter as organic-carbon percent times 1.724; the carbon-to-nitrogen ratio as organic carbon over total nitrogen (both in g/kg).

Attribution

SoilGrids data are released under CC-BY 4.0. Cite Poggio et al. (2021), SoilGrids 2.0, SOIL 7, 217-240, doi:10.5194/soil-7-217-2021 .

See also

spatial_N_balance, farm_balance

Examples

if (FALSE) { # requireNamespace("geodata", quietly = TRUE) && interactive()
aoi <- sf::st_read(system.file("extdata/cerzoo_field.geojson", package = "agrinutri"))
soil <- soilgrids_input(aoi, crs_out = 32632)
n <- spatial_N_balance(soil, expected_yield_tons_ha = 9,
                       crop = "Grano tenero FF (granella)",
                       ccp = "Spring-summer crop 100-130 days",
                       winter_rain = 150, start_spring_rain = 0,
                       prev_crop = "Maize stalks buried")
}
